observation.visible_scene: Close-up of a car tire resting on a concrete surface, with a small clear plastic bottle/container packed with multicolored water-beads lying under the tread. The wheel has a silver hubcap with protruding tabs and the sidewall lettering 'KRYSTA'. A white bumper is partly visible at the top-left in the earliest frames.
visible_changes: The tire rotates and translates leftward across the frame throughout the excerpt; the white bumper at top-left moves out of view, indicating the car is moving relative to a stationary camera rather than the camera panning.

The bottle stays in roughly the same screen position while the tire rolls over it; its colorful bead-filled body visibly flattens and spreads horizontally (the oval of beads grows wider from a compact blob to an elongated shape).

The gray rounded end of the bottle on the left becomes progressively covered by the advancing tread and is no longer visible by the middle-to-late frames (occlusion by the tire, not the bottle vanishing).
Colored droplets and smears appear on the concrete to the left of the bottle in the later frames, consistent with material being squeezed out as the tire presses on it.
The hubcap tabs and sidewall text persist as the same object features, only changing orientation/position as the wheel rolls.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the bottle came to be under the tire (no placement is shown; crushing is already underway at the first frame).
What happens after the tire fully passes the bottle (the segment ends with the tire still in contact, so the final state of the bottle is not shown).
Whether the container ruptures completely or only leaks.
uncertain_details: Exact rotation sense of the wheel and precise speed of the car are inferred from translation, not directly measured.
The material identity of the colorful contents (water beads vs. small candies) is not certain.
The ground speckle pattern is too uniform to confirm the camera is perfectly still versus a very slight drift.
